newsitem.title: CHINA: HK warns public to stay home as skies open up.
newsitem.headline: HK warns public to stay home as skies open up.

text.p: Hong Kong's weather took a distinct turn for the worse on Tuesday, only hours into Chinese rule, as the skies opened up and authorities issued a severe rainstorm warning.
Hong Kong was hit by driving rain just hours after Britain's Prince Charles handed over the territory to Chinese President Jiang Zemin at midnight (1600 GMT) on June 30.

The inclement weather did nothing to prevent thousands of people from turning out to welcome People's Liberation Army troops as they arrived in armoured personnel carriers, trucks, coaches and a flotilla of navy vessels.
The Hong Kong Observatory said more than 100 millimetres (four inches) of rain fell over Hong Kong in a two-hour period.
"Because of seriously flooded roads and inclement weather conditions, you are advised to take shelter in a safe place and stay there," the observatory said.
"Do not attempt to travel until the rainstorm black warning is no longer in force and traffic conditions have improved."
Hong Kong's hilly and built-up terrain makes it prone to landslips in heavy rain.
Despite the bad weather, Jiang and other mainland VIPs will be able to fly out of Hong Kong on Tuesday, an aviation official said.
Richard Siegel, director of the Civil Aviation Department, said Kai Tak airport was open and operational "within the constraints of the weather".
